title: Pair encoding via doubling
statement: For any two bit strings $x$ and $y$, encoding the pair $(x,y)$ gives the concatenation of the string obtained by writing each bit of $x$ twice, the separator $01$, and $y$.
replaced:
For all bit strings $x$ and $y$, the self-delimiting pair encoding
$\langle x, y\rangle$ equals the concatenation
\[
  \langle x, y\rangle = \mathrm{dbl}(x)\; 0\, 1\; y,
\]
where $\mathrm{dbl}(x)$ is $x$ with every bit written twice in succession,
followed by the separator bits $0$ then $1$, followed by $y$ verbatim.
